stemMd: The passage suggests that two merchants on similar routes could appear differently in formal insurance records because

options.label: A
options.textMd: all network members refused any insurance policy.

options.label: B
options.textMd: one was prohibited from trading by the historians.

options.label: C
options.textMd: formal records include only the safest possible voyages.

options.label: D
options.textMd: their ships necessarily faced different weather.

options.label: E
options.textMd: one had access to a reciprocal network unavailable to the other.

explanationMd: Network access changes available risk-management choices even holding route characteristics similar. It can therefore influence who enters formal records.

distractorRationale.c: The direction of selection is not fixed that way.
distractorRationale.d: Similar routes need not imply the particular weather difference asserted.
distractorRationale.b: The historians do not regulate the merchants.
distractorRationale.a: A universal refusal is not stated.
